title: FEI Tribunal Decision — FEI Tribunal Decision Settlement Agreement Case C25-0019 2025BS04 FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN VALLEJO PR
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY FEI TRIBUNAL
19 December 2025
in the matter of
Mr. Arturo Parada Vallejo – Person Responsible (the “PR”) (Ref. C25-0019)
(FEI Case number: 2025/BS04) FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Ms Diane Pitts, (USA), Sole Panel Member (the “Panel”)
FEI Tribunal reference: C25-0019 PARADA
Horse/Passport: FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN /106CI24/MEX
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Arturo PARADA VALLEJO/ 10095117/MEX
Event/Date: CSIO4* - Wellington, FL, Equestrian Center (USA), 25.02.2025-02.03.2025
Event/ID: 2025_CI_0407_S_S_01
Date of sample collection: 02.03.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Lamotrigine
Bar Code No.: 1488305
1

I. INTRODUCTION
1. This Decision pertains to the FEI case (2025/BS04) (FELLOW VAN'T MOERVEN) (the “Horse”).
In respect of this case, the FEI notified the PR of a violation of Article 2.1 (The presence of a
Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) of the Equine Anti-
doping Rules (the “EADRs”) based on the Laboratory's Adverse Analytical Finding (the “AAF”)
of Lamotrigine in the Horse's Sample collected at the CSIO4* - Wellington, FL, Equestrian
Center (USA), 25.02.2025-02.03.2025 (the “Event”).
2. A Settlement Agreement between the FEI and the PR was agreed by the Parties on 10
November 2025 (the “Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement and the Exhibits
thereto are hereby incorporated herein by reference.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions:
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January
2025 (“GRs”).
▪ Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations, 4th edition, effective
1 January 2025 (“EADCMRs”). The EADCM Rules are divided into the Equine Anti-
Doping Rules (the “EADRs”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the
“ECM Rules”).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 3rd Edition, 1 February 2025 (“the IRs”).
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21st November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
III. PARTIES
3. Mr. Arturo PARADA VALLEJO (FEI ID 10095117), the PR in accordance with Article 118.3
of the GRs, is an Athlete in the discipline of Jumping for Mexico (the “MEX-NF”), who
competed with the Horse at the Event.
4. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and Para-Driving,
Endurance and Vaulting.
2

IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
5. The Horse was tested during the Event, and the analysis of the urine and blood samples
revealed the presence of Lamotrigine, an anticonvulsant used to control seizures and
mood changes in bipolar disorder. Lamotrigine is classified as a Banned Substance
under the 2025 FEI Equine Prohibited Substances List (the “List”).
6. By Notification Letter dated 22 April 2025 (the “Notification Letter”), the FEI informed the
PR of a potential violation of Article 2.1 of the EADRs, the Presence of a Banned Substance
and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample based on the findings of
Lamotrigine in the samples. The PR was also notified in said letter that he was
provisionally suspended under Article 7.4.1 of the EADRs, and the Horse was also
provisionally suspended for two months until 21 June 2025.
7. The Notification Letter also outlined the following options to the PR that:
• within 10 days of the Notification Letter, he may request the B sample analysis;
• within 20 days of the Notification Letter, he may admit the violation and receive an
automatic six (6) month reduction in the Period of Ineligibility;
• alternatively, within 20 days of the Notification Letter, he may challenge the violation
and/or consequences;
• that he has the right to a Preliminary Hearing;
• that he may enter into a case resolution agreement with the FEI;
• that he has the option to provide substantial assistance;
• that he may ask for the automatic disqualification of his results.
8. By letter dated 29 April 2025, the PR requested for the B Sample to be analysed. The
urine and blood samples (Sample no 1488305) were sent to the FEI-approved Hong Kong
Jockey Club Racing Laboratory (the “Laboratory”) in Sha Tin, NT (HKG), for analysis. The B
Sample analysis of the urine and blood sample confirmed the presence of Lamotrigine.
The PR was notified of the results of the B Sample analysis by letter dated 26 May 2025.
9. The PR submitted that the Lamotrigine detected in the Horse’s sample on 2 March 2025,
more likely than not came from the inadvertent transfer of Lamotrigine residue from a
colleague of his cousin, who attended the Event and helped with the horse on the day in
question. The colleague inadvertently transferred the substance when he broke the
Lamotrigine medication in his hands to ingest it (which he took to treat his post-accident
seizures). The FEI expert confirmed that such explanation was scientifically plausible.
3

10. On 11 June 2025, the PR requested the urgent lifting of the provisional suspension in
accordance with Article 7.4.4 (ii) of the EADR. The FEI consented to that request and
confirmed that the parties were currently in negotiations to enter into a no-fault
agreement.
11. On 14 June 2025, the Panel issued the Operative Award and lifted the provisional
suspension with effect from midnight CET.
12. On 13 November 2025, the FEI submitted the Settlement Agreement with Exhibits for
the approval of the FEI Tribunal (the “Tribunal”) and requested for a FEI Tribunal Panel
to be appointed for the purpose or review and approval of said Settlement Agreement.
13. On 5 December 2025, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a sole
panel member (the “Panel”) to adjudicate and approve this case. The Parties were
asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the Panel by 9 December 2025.
On 8 and 9 December 2025, the FEI and PR, respectively, provided no objections to
the constitution of the Panel.
V. ACCEPTED TERMS
14. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs and is
subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
NOW, THEREFORE, THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED TO THE FOLLOWING
TERMS FOR THE CLOSURE OF THE PROCEEDINGS:
15. In the matter of the Adverse Analytical Finding related to the samples, which were collected
from the PR’s horse FELLOW VAN’T MOERVEN in the CSIO4*-L in Wellington, FL (USA),
between 25 February and 2 March 2025, the PR and the FEI agree in accordance with the
Article 10.8.2 of the EADR on the following:
(a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 EADR (The presence of a Banned Substance
and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample);
(b) The PR established, on a balance of probabilities, how Lamotrigine entered the Horse’s
system;
4

(c) The PR has established that he bore No Fault or Negligence for the rule violation in
accordance with the Article 10.5 EADR;
(d) The period of Ineligibility imposed on the PR shall therefore be eliminated;
(e) The results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified, with all
resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes, in
accordance with the Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADR;
(f) The PR’s Horse was Provisionally Suspended for the period of two (2) months (until 21
June 2025);
(g) The PR shall not incur any fine;
(h) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with these
proceedings;
(i) No other Sanctions will apply in this case;
(j) In accordance with Article 10.9.2 of the EADR, this violation of the EADR shall not be
considered a prior violation for the purpose of Article 10.9 (Multiple Violations) of the
EADR.
16. This agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and is subject
to the approval of the FEI Tribunal. The Parties hereby kindly request that the FEI
Tribunal issue a Decision incorporating the terms of this agreement.
17. In accordance with the Article 10.8.2 of the EADR, the Decision by the FEI to enter or not
enter into a case resolution agreement, and the amount of the reduction to, and the starting
date of, the period of Ineligibility and the confirmation of the case resolution agreement by
the FEI Tribunal are not subject to appeal under Article 13 of the EADR.
18. The parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADR, the Decision
will be made public by the FEI.
19. The terms set out in this agreement have been agreed as a full and final settlement of all
claims relating to the subject-matter of these proceedings. Accordingly, any and all other
claims for relief that any party might otherwise have made against another in relation to the
subject matter of these proceedings are released and discharged unconditionally, and they
may not be pursued in any form hereafter.
VI. DECISION
1. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
159 of the GRs, the EADRs and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member of the MEX-NF,
5

which is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EADRs.
2. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement and
the Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel accepts that the FEI found that the PR had
established, on a balance of probabilities, how Lamotrigine entered the Horse’s system.
3. The Tribunal further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on the terms for
the closure of the proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, as detailed
under Section V of this Decision.
4. The Tribunal confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement comply with
the EADRs and finds no grounds to object thereto.
5. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADRs this Final
Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the Settlement Agreement
are a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject matter of these
proceedings.
6. The Settlement Agreement and this Decision are not subject to appeal under Article 13
of the EADRs.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
b. The NF of the PR: Yes
c. Any other: No
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
_______________________________________________________________
Ms Diane Pitts (USA), Sole Panel Member
6
